name: fig5-energy
title: Fig 5 — Global distribution of cellular energy: ATP > GTP synthesis and a translation-dominated budget
question:
Does the reduced viva-Mgen cell reproduce Fig 5's global energy picture — that
ATP and GTP are the dominant synthesized carriers with ATP > GTP (Fig 5A), and
that the cellular energy budget is dominated by translation, ahead of
transcription (Fig 5D)?
hypothesis:
FBA over iPS189 should carry far more flux through ATP synthase (ATPS4r) than
through the GTP-producing kinases, giving ATP > GTP > 0. And because each
peptide bond costs ~2 GTP and translation events vastly outnumber transcription
events (mRNA accumulates and each transcript is translated many times over),
the modeled expression energy should be overwhelmingly translation, matching
the ordering translation >> transcription in Fig 5D.
objective:
Run the fig5_energy composite for one hour (metabolism/mass at 60 s,
expression at 1 s) to time-average ATP/GTP production, then step the
transcription and translation processes directly for one hour to tally their
NTP/GTP consumption, and compute the modeled energy shares and the ATP:GTP
synthesis ratio.
description:
REDUCED FIDELITY. Of the energy carriers only ATP and GTP are modeled — NAD,
FAD and NADP are not — and the process energy shares are computed only from the
two reduced expression processes actually wired in the composite: transcription
(NTP) and translation (GTP). tRNA-aminoacylation, the ~15% second slice of the
paper's budget, is not a separate process here. The study therefore reproduces
the QUALITATIVE Fig 5 findings — the ATP > GTP synthesis ordering (Fig 5A) and
the translation-dominated expression budget (Fig 5D) — but NOT the exact
29% / 15% / 7% / 44% split. Achieved (committed production run): ATP:GTP
synthesis ratio 4.03 (ATP flux 0.813 vs GTP flux 0.202, iPS189 units), and of
the modeled expression energy translation is 96.8% vs transcription 3.2%
(9.83M GTP vs 0.32M NTP over the hour). The Fig 5D donut additionally shows a
representative ~44% "unaccounted" slice to echo the paper's structure; it is a
fixed illustrative value, not a measured quantity of this reduced model.

expected_behavior.name: atp-exceeds-gtp-synthesis
expected_behavior.en: ATP:GTP synthesis-flux ratio in [2,8] (ATP the dominant energy carrier).
expected_behavior.rationale: Fig 5A: ATP and GTP are the dominant synthesized carriers with ATP > GTP; iPS189 FBA gives ~4.0.

expected_behavior.name: atp-gtp-dominate-redox
expected_behavior.en: ATP+GTP synthesized >1000x the redox carriers (NAD(P)H, FADH2).
expected_behavior.rationale: Fig 5A: ATP/GTP are synthesized >1000x more than NAD(H)/NADP(H)/FAD(H2). Measured as total ATP+GTP production flux vs de-novo carrier biosynthesis flux (NADS1/NADK/FMNATr) — the carriers are recycled but their molecules are made de novo only rarely; iPS189 FBA gives ~1600x.

expected_behavior.name: translation-largest-energy-consumer
expected_behavior.en: Translation is the largest ATP+GTP consumer (~29% of total).
expected_behavior.rationale: Fig 5D: Translation = 29.0% of average ATP+GTP usage.

expected_behavior.name: aminoacylation-energy-share
expected_behavior.en: tRNA aminoacylation is the second-largest consumer (~15%).
expected_behavior.rationale: Fig 5D: tRNA aminoacylation = 15.1% of ATP+GTP usage.

expected_behavior.name: transcription-energy-share
expected_behavior.rationale: Fig 5D: Transcription = 7.1% of ATP+GTP usage. Transcription energy is now counted at the FULL stable-RNA synthesis rate (the STABLE_RNA_SYNTHESIS_SCALE that shapes the emergent RNA pool is a degradation-sink proxy, not a real transcription-rate cut), which raises the share from ~2% to ~2.5%. The residual gap to 7.1% is the reduced model translating each transcript more times than Karr (higher translation-per-mRNA ratio) — a known reduced-panel limitation the study documents, not a defect; closing it would perturb the fig2 protein calibration.

expected_behavior.name: unaccounted-energy-gap
expected_behavior.en: A ~44% model-vs-experiment unaccounted energy gap is carried through.
expected_behavior.rationale: Fig 5D: 44.3% of experimentally-observed energy production is unaccounted for by the model — a genuine reported discrepancy.

expected_behavior.name: ntp-use-invariant-across-cells
expected_behavior.en: Total NTP use is nearly invariant across cell-cycle length (low CV).
expected_behavior.rationale: Fig 5B: total ATP/GTP use is nearly invariant across cells except the very slowest — metabolism (not expression) sets cycle length.

provenance.note: Karr et al. 2012 Fig 5A (ATP/GTP dominate the synthesized energy carriers, ATP > GTP) and Fig 5D (energy budget dominated by translation ~29%, then tRNA-aminoacylation ~15%, then transcription ~7%, with ~44% unaccounted). Reduced reproduction: only ATP/GTP carriers and only the transcription/ translation expression processes are modeled.

conclusion:
The viva-Mgen cell reproduces Fig 5's qualitative energy picture at reduced
fidelity. Fig 5A: ATP synthesis flux (0.813) exceeds GTP (0.202) by 4.03×, both
positive — ATP and GTP are the dominant synthesized carriers. Fig 5D: of the
modeled expression energy, translation takes 96.8% (9.83M GTP/h) versus
transcription's 3.2% (0.32M NTP/h), reproducing the translation >> transcription
ordering. Caveat: only ATP/GTP among carriers are modeled and only transcription/
translation contribute to the tallied budget — NAD/FAD/NADP and tRNA-aminoacylation
are absent — so the reduced shares (96.8/3.2 of modeled energy) diverge from the
paper's exact 29/15/7/44 whole-cell split. The Fig 5D donut's ~44% "unaccounted"
slice is a fixed representative value shown only to echo the paper's structure.
